page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is a high-capacity server instance powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 192 virtual CPUs mapped to 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 720 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 3.75 GB per core. The processor runs at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and features a 260 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 165,332.95 and a PassMark CPU score of 115,368.08. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 577.03 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 247.9 GB/sec for writes. The instance excels in parallel processing workloads, as demonstrated by its top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 20,711.0 and software compilation score of 61,778.0. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance falling into the average tier at 2,098.49.

The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which accelerate cryptographic and mathematical operations. This is reflected in strong LLM inference speeds, particularly for medium and large models, such as 44.38 tokens/sec for medium model text generation. Given the high core count, substantial memory, and lack of local storage, this instance is optimized for large-scale compute-intensive workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, high-throughput web serving, and memory-bound parallel processing tasks that rely on network-attached storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is a high-capacity, general-purpose server instance featuring 192 vCPUs and 720 GB of RAM. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processors running at 2.3 GHz, this x86_64 architecture instance provides 96 physical cores with hyper-threading. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the top tier for multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, and parallel processing, though single-core performance remains average. Supported by advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, it delivers strong performance in cryptography, software compilation, and large-scale LLM inference. The c4-standard-192 is highly suited for compute-intensive multi-threaded workloads, high-throughput web serving, and database operations.
